candidates.name: @base-ui/react
candidates.maintenance: active; latest 1.7.0 published 2026-08-04; pinned here at 1.6.0
candidates.decision_rationale: Operator decision D1 keeps Base UI, overriding the KnowMe standard §6.1/§6.3 which name Shadcn UI as the required owner for general controls. This is a RECORDED DIVERGENCE from the standard, not compliance with it. Base UI is technically adequate for Flat 2.0: it is unstyled, so no default border/shadow chrome arrives to be removed, and its data-attribute state model (data-checked, data-highlighted, data-popup-open) maps onto the standard §3.2 rule that state be a fill change. It is NOT established that Base UI is less total work than shadcn — shadcn copies editable source into the repo rather than shipping CSS as a dependency, so its stripping cost is a one-time edit of owned files. No effort comparison was performed.

evidence.claim: Already migrated in code: 0 @radix-ui imports in frontend/src, 34 files importing @base-ui/react.
OpenSpec base-ui-foundation is 24/24 complete; base-ui-composition-patterns 0/40, base-ui-icon-migration 0/28, base-ui-verification 0/33 remain.
Context7 /mui/base-ui/v1.6.0 handbook: 'Base UI components are unstyled and do not bundle CSS.'
npm view @base-ui/react version -> 1.7.0; time.modified 2026-08-04.

risks: DIVERGENCE: KnowMe standard §6.1 and §6.3 (line 227) name Shadcn UI as required owner for general controls. D1 overrides this; the divergence must be recorded in the vendored standard's header, which currently claims §6.3 applies verbatim.
Goal 4 still names 'shadcn' and must be amended, or every downstream change reads as off-spec.

27 declared @radix-ui/* packages have no direct src imports, BUT cmdk, @assistant-ui/react, @assistant-ui/react-markdown and storybook depend on Radix transitively. A prune requires a dependency-graph check, not a declaration sweep.
Remaining base-ui-* work (0/40, 0/28, 0/33) becomes this phase's scope.

candidates.name: tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/vite
candidates.decision_rationale: Plan §4.2 requires deleting tailwind.config.ts and postcss.config.js and moving tokens into @theme. Tailwind 4 compiles theme variables into real CSS custom properties on :root, which is the token model KnowMe standard §4.1 specifies (complete colors, not channel triplets). NOT a small migration: the hsl(var()) channel indirection appears 237 times across 12 files, not 15.

evidence.claim: Context7 /tailwindlabs/tailwindcss.com upgrade guide: vite.config.ts gains the @tailwindcss/vite plugin; @theme replaces the JS config; theme vars compile to :root custom properties.
npm view @tailwindcss/vite version -> 4.3.3, version-matched to tailwindcss 4.3.3.
Measured migration surface: 3 @apply directives (index.css:290,300,326), 121-line tailwind.config.ts, 429-line index.css, and 237 hsl(var()) occurrences across 12 files.

risks: 237 hsl(var()) occurrences, ~175 of them inside the 13 admin pages (models-page 60, memory-page 56, cost-dashboard 31, skills-page 15, compiler-page 13). This materially raises the cost of the admin-page workstream.
The 3 @apply directives reference legacy shadcn token names (bg-background, ring-ring) that must be renamed to KnowMe token names.
index.css:9 records a deliberate operator decision of 2026-07-21 to keep the Tailwind 3 channel mechanism. This phase reverses it; the reversal must be explicit in the change record.

candidates.name: rehype-sanitize
candidates.decision_rationale: HARD PREREQUISITE for rehype-raw under A-3. There is no current vulnerability: without rehype-raw, react-markdown escapes raw HTML by default, verified empirically for both renderer sites. But plan §7.2 deliberately ENABLES rehype-raw so agents can emit inline SVG, converting model output into a live trust boundary. rehype-sanitize must land in the SAME change as rehype-raw; splitting them ships a window in which agent output can inject script.

evidence.claim: Absent from package.json. Current renderer enhanced-markdown-text.tsx:71 passes only remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]} with no rehype chain.
Second renderer admin/pages/skills-page.tsx:84 uses bare ReactMarkdown with remarkGfm only — same escaping property, also currently safe.
Plan §7.2 requires rehypeSanitize immediately after rehypeRaw on every path; sanitize schema is a single reviewed file with XSS fixtures.

risks: Must not be sequenced separately from rehype-raw.
Schema too strict breaks legitimate agent SVG; too loose reopens XSS. Requires unit tests with XSS fixtures.

components/ui/chart.tsx:96 uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML for CSS custom-property injection from developer-authored ChartConfig. Benign as configured; the invariant to enforce is that ChartConfig.color/.theme never accept model or user input.

candidates.name: remark-math + rehype-katex + katex + remark-breaks + rehype-raw
candidates.maintenance: active; all mainstream unified/remark ecosystem packages
candidates.decision_rationale: Plan §7.2 fixes the exact plugin chain. All are absent today. KaTeX additionally requires its stylesheet and font loading strategy, which is not yet specified anywhere.

evidence.claim: Measured absent from package.json: remark-math, rehype-katex, katex, rehype-raw, dompurify. Only remark-gfm@^4.0.1 present.
Plan §7.2 specifies remarkChain = [remarkGfm, remarkBreaks, remarkMath] and rehypeChain = [rehypeRaw, [rehypeSanitize, schema], rehypeKatex].

risks: KaTeX CSS and font loading strategy unspecified; naive import adds render-blocking CSS and font weight.
rehype-raw is the plugin that opens the trust boundary — see cand-003.

candidates.name: mermaid + shiki
candidates.decision_rationale: Plan §7.1/§7.3 require one shared MermaidBlock (a ```mermaid fence and a mermaid artifact must render identically) and Shiki superseding highlight.js. Both must be lazy-loaded via import() and must never enter the initial chunk.

evidence.claim: Both absent from package.json. highlight.js is also not installed, so there is nothing to remove.
Build already emits a >1100 kB chunk warning BEFORE adding either library.
Plan §3.2 lists vendor-mermaid and vendor-shiki as separate manualChunks; §7.1 requires mermaid securityLevel 'strict' and finalize-only rendering.

risks: Bundle weight against goal 12's 250 KB gzip initial-JS budget, which is already at risk given the existing >1100 kB chunk warning.
Mermaid must never render mid-stream (partial fences fail to parse) — finalize-only per plan §7.4.
Every renderer needs an error boundary and source fallback (plan §7.1 rule 3).

candidates.name: @electric-sql/pglite
candidates.decision_rationale: No dependency change required — already present at latest with the live extension available in node_modules. The gap is schema (no run or run_event table), not tooling. This is the critical path for the phase's headline feature: the run-trace bar, timeline, inspector, and replay all depend on a persisted append-only event record.

evidence.claim: Schema today is threads, messages, schema_migrations only; grep run_event returns 0.
Threads and messages ARE written incrementally (chat-message-store.ts, thread-registry-store.ts), so the incremental-persistence pattern is already proven in this codebase.
npm view @electric-sql/pglite version -> 0.5.4, matching the installed range.

risks: Plan §5.2 proposes deleting the hand-rolled outbox in favour of PEM's startLocalFirstGraph — unverified, see open question OQ-PEM-API.
Multi-tab ownership: standard §6.2 prefers a shared worker; not currently used.

candidates.name: @prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management
candidates.decision_rationale: Keep as-is. The plan's 'pin an exact next version' risk row assumes npm resolution; this repo vendors PEM as a pnpm workspace package, so drift is governed by the submodule pointer instead. Pinning to an npm 'next' tag would be a regression from the current setup. Required owner per standard §6.3.

evidence.claim: 56 files already import it; package.json resolves it as workspace:*.
KnowMe standard §6.2: 'TanStack Query is not part of the KnowMe architecture'; PEM 3.x is the required entity/reactivity layer.

risks: OQ-PEM-API: createPGlitePersistenceAdapter, startLocalFirstGraph and registerEntityFromSql are named by plan §5.2 but unverified in the vendored version. Verify before any change depends on them.

candidates.name: @assistant-ui/react
candidates.decision_rationale: Required owner per standard §6.3 for thread, composer, attachments, message actions, streaming lifecycle and thread list — contractual, not preference. Defer the 0.14 to 0.15 bump to its own change: the imported surface is narrow so the bump is low-risk, but it is not a prerequisite for the rebuild and sequencing it separately keeps the diff readable.

evidence.claim: Only 4 files import it; imported symbols are useExternalStoreRuntime, AssistantRuntimeProvider, AppendMessage, ThreadMessageLike.
No file mixes @assistant-ui and @base-ui imports — the layers are cleanly separated today.
npm view @assistant-ui/react version -> 0.15.8; time.modified 2026-08-06.

risks: Standard §6.2 warns presence is not satisfaction: primitives must be mounted at the real interaction boundary. Verify actual mounting rather than dependency presence.
@assistant-ui/react depends on Radix transitively — relevant to the cand-001 prune.

candidates.name: @tanstack/react-virtual
candidates.decision_rationale: Plan §8.5 requires the run-trace timeline to virtualize past ~200 rows, and goal 12 sets a budget of a 500-event run rendering in <=100ms. Nothing virtualization-capable is installed. Marked REFERENCE rather than ADOPT because the choice was not researched to tier-2/3 depth in this stage and should be confirmed against the actual timeline component shape (variable row heights, nested tree) before adoption. Note @tanstack/react-table IS already installed, so the TanStack ecosystem is not new to the repo — but react-table is not a virtualizer.

evidence.claim: No virtualization library in package.json; @tanstack/react-table ^8.21.3 is present but does not provide row virtualization.
Plan §8.5 requires timeline virtualization past ~200 rows; goal 12 budgets a 500-event trace render at <=100ms.

risks: UNRESEARCHED AT DEPTH — this is a genuine gap in this analyze stage. The plan stage must not treat it as a settled adoption.
The trace timeline is hierarchical (plan §8.5 tree), which constrains virtualizer choice more than a flat list would.

candidates.name: cmdk
candidates.decision_rationale: Already installed and used; plan §6.1 and goal 9 require a command palette in the shell. Flagged REFERENCE rather than adopt because cmdk depends on Radix transitively, which interacts directly with the cand-001 prune and with D1's move to Base UI. Base UI is likely to have its own equivalent primitive; that comparison was not made in this stage.

evidence.claim: cmdk is present in package.json and depends on Radix transitively, so it survives any @radix-ui declaration prune.
Plan §6.1 lists command-palette.tsx in the app shell directory tree.

risks: Keeping cmdk keeps Radix in the bundle after D1 moved primitives to Base UI — a mixed-primitive shell.
Not compared against a Base UI equivalent. The plan stage should resolve this before building the shell.

The KnowMe standard's design-quality expectations treat data visualisation as part of the design system, which may or may not be satisfiable by restyling recharts under Flat 2.0.

evidence.claim: recharts ^3.10.1 installed and imported by 2 files including components/ui/chart.tsx.
Plan §8.3 requires chart-block.tsx as a registered block renderer.

risks: UNRESEARCHED AT DEPTH — carried as an open item, not a decision.
components/ui/chart.tsx injects CSS custom properties via dangerouslySetInnerHTML; any chart decision must preserve the invariant that its config never accepts model input.
